key_insight: Adding human gesture as a parallel instruction modality to Vision-Language-Action models enables robots to resolve spatial ambiguity in cluttered or multi-object scenes, producing more precise action grounding and manipulation.
problem_solved: VLA systems that rely only on text struggle to disambiguate referents in complex scenes with multiple similar objects and offer limited, natural multimodal interaction; GesVLA integrates gestures to clarify spatial intent and improve action selection.
method: Encode gesture features (hand pose, pointing direction, spatial cue) and embed them into the shared vision-language-action latent space.
Fuse gesture, visual, and textual inputs via a multimodal attention / transformer module to disambiguate referents and produce action-conditioned representations.
Train with paired gesture–image–language–action data using alignment/contrastive objectives and action supervision so the model maps multimodal instructions to executable policies.
impact: GesVLA makes human-robot instruction more robust and intuitive by leveraging natural gestures to remove spatial ambiguity — accelerating deployment of general-purpose manipulation agents in real-world HRI and industrial settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: camera image + text + hand gesture → multimodal fusion → action output (robot arm), with arrows showing information flow.
Before/after scene: identical cluttered tabletop with two similar objects, showing ambiguous text-only instruction vs. resolved instruction with pointing gesture.
Embedding visualization (e.g., 2D projection) showing separation of object referents when gesture is included vs. overlapping clusters without gesture.
Icon set: hand/gesture, speech bubble/text, camera/image, robot arm to quickly convey the multimodal components.
paper_title: GesVLA: Gesture-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model Embedded Representations
paper_authors: Wenxuan Guo, Ziyuan Li, Meng Zhang, Yichen Liu, Yimeng Dong
